title: Three layers: meaning, background, data
source: Rector, PEN&PAD, GALEN & GRAIL, DRAFT Nov 2026, pp. 1–3.

steps.title: Meaning: a definition
steps.body: The meaning layer is what a description-logic reasoner can use: statements that are universally true within the scope of the application. A definition is one of the three kinds the draft lists.
steps.task: Read the Definition section. A dotted word such as which can be hovered or tapped for a short explanation.

quote.text: Definitions – Pericarditis = Inflammation of the Pericardium

steps.dump: In this dump the published definition is “InflammationLesion which hasSpecificLocation Pericardium”. That is the draft’s example in OpenGALEN’s names. The shorter wording is not itself a concept name here.

steps.title: Meaning: a universal
steps.body: A universal says something of every member of a class. In this graph Vertebrate is a parent of Bird, so Bird is classified under Vertebrate. The same list in the draft includes a static-within-scope fact about Paris. Paris and France are not concepts in this terminology. This step follows Bird only.

quotes.text: Universals – (All) Hands are parts of upper extremities, (All) Birds are Vertebrates
Paris is the capital of France

steps.dump: In this dump, Bird’s parents include NonHuman and Vertebrate. There is no concept named Paris and none named France.

steps.title: Background knowledge
steps.body: Background knowledge is a different layer from meaning. The draft says it may be generally true without being necessarily true, and that authors are tempted to include too much of it in the ontology. The penicillin line below is one of its examples of a useful generalisation. It is not a definition in this dump.
steps.task: Read the definition. It is about staining, not about penicillin.

quotes.text: Statements that may be/are generally/… true but are not necessarily true
The classic manifestation confusing meaning and background knowledge is the question “How do I say ‘may’ on OWL?”.
Useful Generalisations – (Most) Gram positive bacteria sensitiveTo (Most) Penicillin.
GALEN represented generic background knowledge as “extrinsics” which were ignored by the classifier but available to applications and inherited by default.

steps.dump: In this dump, GramPositiveBacterium is defined as “Bacterium which isActedOnSpecificallyBy GramPositiveStaining”. Penicillin is a separate concept. This browser does not show the sensitiveTo sentence as a definition of either concept.

steps.title: Higher-order knowledge
steps.body: Higher-order knowledge was left out of the terminology except in comments. A statement about the class Gorilla is not a statement about each gorilla, and a description-logic reasoner cannot treat it as one.
steps.task: Look through Parents. The endangered-species sentence is not one of them.

quotes.text: Higher order knowledge was excluded except in comments.
“Gorilla is an endangered species”. This is a statement about the class/species Gorilla, not about “all gorillas”.
They cannot be reasoned over by a DL reasoner.

steps.dump: In this dump, Gorilla’s parents include Hominidae and NonHumanPrimate. Nothing here states that the species is endangered: there is no such parent and no such definition.

steps.title: The data layer is out of scope
steps.body: The data layer was excluded from PEN&PAD and GALEN. The model is about meaning and knowledge. A statement about one patient is not a description-logic necessity, so it is not a node in this graph. The concept on screen is a class in the terminology, not a chart entry.
steps.task: Nothing to click. This graph has no patient, no encounter, and no record.

quotes.text: Excluded from PEN&PAD and GALEN themselves.
The GALEN model was about meaning and knowledge, not data.
Statements about individual patients (data) do not follow DL semantics because they can never be “necessary”.

steps.dump: In this dump there is no patient, encounter, or record. Where a record would start is a later chapter and is not part of this version.
